tabs.name: GitHub Copilot
tabs.rulesContent:
## Sonatype MCP

When handling code related to dependencies, package management, or software supply chain security, always prioritize Sonatype MCP tools. Use the available MCP tools to research versions, check for vulnerabilities, and get recommendations before adding or updating any dependencies.

ideConfigs.description: Add the following to the global VS Code mcp.json or create a .vscode/mcp.json in your workspace.
ideConfigs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname. Switch to Agent mode in Copilot chat to access MCP tools.

ideConfigs.description: In Copilot Chat (Agent mode), click the *Tools* icon and add a new server:
ideConfigs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname.

ideConfigs.description: Open Copilot Chat and make sure you are in Agent mode. Then click the tools icon and either browse the registry to install Sonatype MCP Server, or manually add the configuration below in mcp.json.
ideConfigs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname.

ideConfigs.description: Follow these steps to configure MCP in Eclipse:
instructions: Open Copilot chat and ensure you are in Agent mode.
Click the Configure Tools icon, then select Model Context Protocol (MCP).
In the Server Configurations section, add the configuration provided below.
ideConfigs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname.

ideConfigs.description: Xcode does not have built-in GitHub Copilot support. To use Sonatype MCP within Xcode, you must install and use the *GitHub Copilot for Xcode* application, which runs separately from the IDE.
instructions: Download and install GitHub Copilot for Xcode. Sign in and grant required permissions.
In GitHub Copilot for Xcode, click tools, then select MCP.
In MCP Configuration, click Edit Config, then add the configuration below.
ideConfigs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname.

tabs.name: Claude Code
tabs.command:
claude mcp add sonatype-mcp \
  https://YOUR-IQ-SERVER/mcp \
  --transport http \
  --scope user \
  --header "Authorization: Basic <base64(username:password)>"

tabs.name: Codex
tabs.config:
For both methods below, define an environment variable SONATYPE_GUIDE_MCP_CREDENTIALS containing your base64-encoded credentials.

Method 1: Using CLI command

codex mcp add sonatype-mcp --url https://YOUR-IQ-SERVER/mcp --header "Authorization: Basic $SONATYPE_GUIDE_MCP_CREDENTIALS"

Method 2: Manual configuration

Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.sonatype-mcp]
url = "https://YOUR-IQ-SERVER/mcp"

[mcp_servers.sonatype-mcp.headers]
Authorization = "Basic ${SONATYPE_GUIDE_MCP_CREDENTIALS}"
tabs.note: Replace YOUR-IQ-SERVER with your IQ Server hostname.

troubleshooting.issue: MCP server not showing in my AI agent
troubleshooting.solution: Make sure you've added the MCP server using the configuration command. Restart your AI assistant after adding the configuration. Check that the MCP server URL is correctly entered with your IQ Server hostname.

Verify you've added an Authorization header with valid Base64-encoded credentials. Encode as: base64(username:password). Check your network connection and firewall settings. Ensure your IQ Server credentials are correct. If the issue persists, contact your administrator.

This error usually means the MCP client isn't properly installed in your AI assistant. Try reinstalling the MCP configuration. Make sure you're using the latest version of your AI assistant. Restart your AI assistant after configuration.

troubleshooting.issue: Tools not responding or returning errors
troubleshooting.solution: Check your internet connection to IQ Server. Verify your authentication status by trying to authenticate again. Look for error messages in your AI assistant's console or logs. Try removing and re-adding the MCP server configuration.

Verify the IQ Server URL is correct and accessible from your network. Check if IQ Server is running. Ensure you're using HTTPS if IQ Server is configured for secure connections. Contact your administrator if firewall rules may be blocking access.

authHelp.title: Authentication
authHelp.description: Use your IQ Server credentials to authenticate. Encode as base64(username:password) and include in the Authorization header.

optionalHeaders.name: X-Application-Id
optionalHeaders.description: IQ application ID for policy evaluation. When provided, MCP tool responses include policy violations specific to this application.

optionalHeaders.name: X-Stage
optionalHeaders.description: Stage label for policy context (e.g., 'build', 'stage-release', 'develop'). Defaults to 'develop' if not specified.
